name: Gini Coefficient (Two-Segment Lorenz)
description: Approximates the Gini coefficient of inequality from a Lorenz curve modeled as two straight segments through two kink points. The result is one minus twice the area under the piecewise-linear Lorenz curve, ranging from 0 (perfect equality) toward 1 (maximal inequality).
notes: This is a two-segment trapezoidal approximation, not the exact Gini; more kink points give better accuracy. Population and income shares must be cumulative, ordered, and lie between 0 and 1 with x1 < x2.

name: Poverty Gap Index
description: Gives the average shortfall below the poverty line as a share of the line, counting the non-poor as zero (Foster–Greer–Thorbecke with α = 1).
notes: Times the poverty line and population, it is the minimum cost of ending poverty with perfect targeting.

name: Foster–Greer–Thorbecke Poverty Index
description: Generalises poverty measures: α = 0 gives the headcount ratio, α = 1 the poverty gap, α = 2 the squared gap that stresses the poorest.
notes: Used by the World Bank and national statistics offices.

name: Age Dependency Ratio
description: Gives the number of children and older people per 100 people of working age.
notes: Ageing societies see the old-age part rise sharply.
